page_002_excluded: flyleaf matter in a different/modern hand, not the recipe hand
note_on_references: Reference files contain no '---' separator, so structural artifacts (page numbers like '1.', recipe markers like '(1)', '{page break}', and line-break hyphens) remain in the reference and are counted by the script. These are constant across all pages and learners, so per-set and per-round comparisons remain internally valid.

per_set_forward_cer.description: CER of each page's FORWARD transcription vs reference; tests whether the agent reads NEW pages better as its alphabet matures.
per_set_forward_cer.trend: No monotonic improvement. Set 2 is worst (inflated by page 007, a hard swallow-oil/jelly recipe at 15.6%). Set 3 is best (8.63%), a modest gain over set 1 (9.53%). Alphabet maturation yielded only a slight net improvement on new pages, not a steady curve.

post_revision_cer_per_round.description: After each set's revision round, CER of the CURRENT version (latest revision else forward) of every page processed so far, vs references. Cumulative.
post_revision_cer_per_round.trend: Revisions had negligible effect on cumulative CER. Each revision round edited only 1-2 tokens per page; round 1 cumulative CER (9.564%) is essentially identical to the set-1 forward mean (9.528%) and a couple of revisions slightly raised page CER (pages 005, 006) even though they corrected the reading, because the corrected spelling diverged from the reference. Revisiting old flags with a maturer alphabet did not measurably lower CER.

notes.word_substitution_letterform: Largest source of genuine error. On hard tokens the agent guessed a plausible word rather than tracking strokes: ref 'gutts'->hyp 'quills', 'redsage'->'sedauge', 'Cotton'->'Cotten', 'wild thyme'->'rose thyme', 'hearthorne'->'hartshorde', 'whilst'->'make it', 'red rose water'->'see roes water', 'clearest'->garbled. Idiosyncratic herb/drug names ('chissvedes','Cloworthes','Iabenese') left as honest literal flags.
notes.modernization: Recurrent: ref 'you'/'yu' regularized, 'vses'->'uses', 'therto'->'thereto', 'til'->'till', 'Cinament'->'Cynament', 'Cammomile'->'Camemill'. Modern spellings substituted for scribal forms in several places.
notes.minim_errors: Present but minor: nn/u/m confusions inside unfamiliar words (e.g. 'fasrnell' for 'flannell' before revision; 'boorle' for 'boyle').
notes.long_s_l_confusion: A few cases, e.g. initial long-s misread (the 'whore'/'sore' flag on page 014 was a long-s+ho false 'wh', corrected in revision).
notes.punctuation_structural: A large share of raw CER is non-semantic: the agent omits reference page numbers ('1.','8','9'), bracketed recipe-count markers ('(1)','(6)'), '{page break}' lines, and end-of-line hyphens that the reference retains. These inflate every page's CER uniformly and are not reading errors.
notes.revision_behavior: Revisions were honest and conservative: corrected genuine misreadings (flannell, seed pearle, bruses & inwardly, seven, sore, poyson) and refused to overwrite ambiguous strokes with contextually-expected words (sack/each, hoards/hearbs, Masthar moniack). Net CER impact ~0.
